question:
**(Geometric Area Analysis Case Study)**

Three points in the plane are $A(2,3)$, $B(5,7)$, and $C(a,11)$. These correspond to corners of a triangular plot under consideration.

(a) Use the determinant method to write the general formula for the area of triangle $ABC$.

(b) If the area is required to be exactly 20 square units, set up the equation and solve for $a$.
explanation:
(a)
Area of triangle $ABC$:
$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}|\begin{vmatrix}x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1\end{vmatrix}|$
$= \frac{1}{2}|\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 5 & 7 & 1 \\ a & 11 & 1\end{vmatrix}|$
Compute determinant:
Expand along third column:
$= \frac{1}{2}|2(7\times1 - 11\times1) - 3(5\times1 - a\times1) + 1(5\times11 - 7\times a)|$
$= \frac{1}{2}|2(7-11) - 3(5-a) + (55-7a)|$
$= \frac{1}{2}|2(-4) - 3(5-a) + (55-7a)|$
$= \frac{1}{2}|-8 - 15 + 3a + 55 - 7a|$
$= \frac{1}{2}|-8-15+55 + 3a -7a|$
$= \frac{1}{2}|32-4a|$

(b)
Set area = 20:
$\frac{1}{2}|32-4a| = 20$
$|32-4a| = 40$
So $32-4a = 40 \implies a = -2$
Or $32-4a = -40 \implies 4a = 72 \implies a = 18$
So, $a = -2$ or $a = 18$
